title: The Well-Tempered Clavier, Book 1, Fugue 20 in A minor

character.text: Exposition fugue with inversion and stretto; a virtuoso piece

sections.label: Link
sections.summary: Free counterpoint: nothing here is traced to the themes.

sections.label: Link
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject, inverted. Alto: the opening of the subject, inverted. Tenor: free counterpoint. Bass: free counterpoint. Returns in Link (bars 26–27).

sections.label: Link
sections.summary: Soprano: free counterpoint. Alto: a figure from the subject. Tenor: a figure from the subject, inverted.

sections.label: Link
sections.summary: Soprano: free counterpoint. Alto: free counterpoint. Bass: a figure from the subject, inverted.

sections.label: Link
sections.summary: Reworks Link (bar 17) in part, with the soprano's line in the alto, the alto's line in the tenor, a step higher. Soprano: free counterpoint. Alto: a figure from the subject. Tenor: free counterpoint. Bass: free counterpoint.

sections.label: Stretto: Subject in A minor (Soprano); Subject in A minor (Tenor)
Link
sections.summary: Free counterpoint: nothing here is traced to the themes.

sections.label: Stretto: Subject in E minor (Alto); Subject in E minor (Bass)
Episode 1
sections.summary: Soprano: the opening of the subject. Alto: a figure from the subject, inverted (3 times), in a sequence falling by a fourth every half bar. Bass: the opening of the subject (2 times), in a sequence rising by a step every bar.

sections.label: Stretto: Subject in A minor (Tenor); Subject in A minor (Alto)
Episode 2
sections.summary: Reworks the codetta (bar 7) in part, with the soprano's line in the alto, the alto's line in the bass, transposed. Alto: a figure from the subject (2 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted. Tenor: a figure from the subject (2 times) and the opening of the subject and a figure from the subject, inverted. Bass: a figure from the subject, inverted (2 times) and the opening of the subject, inverted.

sections.label: Stretto: Subject in C major (Soprano); Subject in C major (Bass)
Episode 3
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject and the opening of the subject, inverted. Alto: a figure from the subject (2 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted. Tenor: a figure from the subject. Bass: a figure from the subject, inverted.

sections.label: Stretto: Subject in D minor, inverted (Alto); Subject in C major, inverted (Tenor)
Episode 4
sections.summary: Alto: a figure from the subject, inverted and a figure from the subject. Tenor: free counterpoint. Bass: free counterpoint.

sections.label: Stretto: Subject in G major, inverted (Bass); Subject in G major, inverted (Soprano)
Episode 5
sections.summary: Soprano: free counterpoint. Alto: a figure from the subject. Tenor: a figure from the subject and the opening of the subject, inverted. Bass: free counterpoint.

sections.label: Stretto: Subject in A minor, inverted (Soprano); Subject in A minor, inverted (Alto)
Episode 6
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject (5 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted (2 times). Alto: a figure from the subject, inverted (2 times) and the opening of the subject and a figure from the subject, in a sequence rising by a step every half bar. Tenor: the opening of the subject, inverted, in a sequence falling by a third every half bar. Bass: the opening of the subject, inverted.

sections.label: Stretto: Subject in D minor (Bass); Subject in A minor (Tenor); Subject in D minor, inverted (Soprano); Subject in D minor, inverted (Alto)
Episode 7
sections.summary: Soprano: free counterpoint, in a sequence rising by a third every half bar. Alto: free counterpoint, in a sequence rising by a third every half bar. Tenor: free counterpoint, in a sequence rising by a third every half bar.

sections.label: Stretto: Subject in F major, inverted (Bass); Subject in G minor, inverted, rhythm varied (Alto)
Stretto: Subject in D minor, inverted (Tenor); Subject in A major (Alto); Subject in D minor (Soprano)

spans.label: Codetta
spans.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject. Alto: the opening of the subject and a figure from the subject, inverted and a figure from the subject. Returns in Episode 2 (bars 40–42).
